national_raw_news.title: 38 mins ago | National 61 FM Nirmala Sitharaman reiterates India’s focus on economic growth amid global disruptions &...
national_raw_news.content: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has pitched for India’s reform-led growth story to investors at a high-level business roundtable in New York, highlighting the country’s 7.8 per cent economic growth in the first quarter of 2026-27 and improved investment climate. Addressing the roundtable organised by the Consulate General of India in association with Bank of America, Ms Sitharaman said India continues to be the world’s fastest-growing major economy despite global disruptions and challenges, the Finance Ministry said on X today. Moreover, she highlighted a range of reforms, including the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, saying these measures have provided greater regulatory certainty, eased compliance and reduced paperwork under the guidance of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The Finance Minister also said the government has focused on creating capital assets and supporting industry through infrastructure development, particularly in aviation, while also fostering a conducive investment climate, the ministry said. Other focus areas include promoting artificial intelligence and data centres, supporting global capability centres, ensuring credit availability to micro, small and medium enterprises and reducing non-performing assets of banks, she said. Ms Sitharaman also reiterated India’s commitment to fiscal prudence and discipline despite continuing challenges facing the global economy since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic.

national_raw_news.title: 6 hours ago | National 165 PM Narendra Modi calls for greater adoption of water-saving technologies & learning from glo...
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has called for sensitising Urban Local Bodies to the challenges arising from urbanisation, including population growth and future water requirements, and suggested organising similar Chintan Shivirs for Urban Local Bodies. Mr Modi chaired the valedictory session of the two-day National Departmental Summit on Water, organised by the Ministry of Jal Shakti yesterday. He called for greater adoption of water-saving technologies. He also suggested dedicated exhibitions and workshops, including exposure to global best practices, to enable Indian manufacturers and stakeholders to develop and scale efficient solutions. Prime Minister appreciated the intensive two-day deliberations and emphasised that the actionable and time-bound action points emerging from the Summit should be pursued through a continuous process of review and learning. He suggested that the Summit should not remain a one-time exercise and called for a continuous process of review and follow-up. Emphasising Jan Bhagidari, Mr Modi suggested promoting “Jal Utsav” to create greater awareness among people. Prime Minister called for making de-silting a regular programme and developing clear criteria and SOPs for de-silting. On dam safety, he stressed rigorous preparedness before every monsoon, adherence to prescribed precautions and creating awareness among school students, including through suitable incorporation in educational curricula. PM Modi further called for strengthening knowledge and capacity on water management and governance in universities and higher educational institutions. He suggested structured interstate study visits involving public representatives, officials and farmers to facilitate practical learning and replication of successful interventions. Prime Minister called for robust water data governance, with water-sector data brought together, systematically managed, analysed and effectively utilised. He recommended the use of AI for data collection and analysis through a uniform format. He also stressed anticipatory and integrated planning to address water scarcity through suitable utilisation of treated water for agriculture and industrial purposes.

national_raw_news.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly adopts resolution urging Centre to recognise Tamil as HC’s principal language 26 mins ago 24
national_raw_news.content: Tamil Nadu Assembly today unanimously adopted a resolution urging the Union Government to take immediate and necessary action to facilitate the use of Tamil as the principal language of the Madras High Court. Moving the resolution at the State Assembly, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay pointed out that under Section 2 of the Tamil Nādu Official Language Act 1956, Tamil has been declared as the official language, and under Sections 4-A and 4-B of the Act, legal recognition has been provided for recording evidence in Tamil in the civil and criminal courts, tribunals, tent courts and revenue Courts functioning under the High Court. The Chief Minister also noted that under Article 348(2) of the Constitution of India, a constitutional mechanism is provided whereby the Governor of a State, with the previous consent of the President of India, may authorise the use of the official language of the State in the proceedings of the High Court. The resolution passed in the Assembly underlines the need to reconsider the necessity of making Tamil the principal language and establish appropriate procedures for petitions, documents and arguments filed or presented in Tamil, as significant advancements have been made in legal Tamil, translation, e -courts, technology-enabled translation and legal databases. The Statement also mentioned that Artificial intelligence technologies have advanced to the extent that speech in Tamil can be simultaneously rendered and heard in English. The resolution also suggested training in legal Tamil and translation for Judges, advocates and Court Personnel and take all necessary legal measures on proposals to be forwarded by the Governor of the State under Article 348 (2) of the Indian Constitution and Section 7 of the Official Languages Act, 1963. Speaking on the resolution, members from various parties supported the Government and said that this is a definitive move so that a common man can understand his case related arguments happening to him or her.

national_raw_news.title: Two-day Drass Festival to begin tomorrow in Ladakh 2 hours ago 50
national_raw_news.content: In Ladakh, the upcoming two-day Drass Festival, scheduled for September 4 and 5, will provide a major platform to showcase the tourism, cultural and adventure potential of Drass, recently announced as a new district. Speaking to Akashvani, Deputy Commissioner Drass, Imtiyaz Kacho, said the revival of the Drass Festival has assumed special significance following the recent formation of the new district. He said the Drass Festival was organised in the past but had witnessed a gap in recent years. The District Administration has now taken the initiative to revive the festival, even on a modest scale this year, to generate renewed interest and highlight the identity and potential of the newly announced district. DC Imtiyaz Kacho said there is tremendous enthusiasm among the people, with interest and queries pouring in from across Ladakh and outside the Union Territory. He said the District Administration aims to develop Drass as an important tourist destination on the national map by promoting its spectacular natural landscapes, rich culture, heritage, adventure tourism and traditional sports. The Drass Festival will feature a wide range of activities, including eco-adventure and nature tours, visits to heritage sites, Horse Polo, Tent Pegging, cultural programmes and youth activities. The festival will also focus strongly on youth engagement, providing school and college students platforms to showcase their hidden talents through cultural, sporting and other extracurricular activities. Being organised under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan, the festival will include awareness programmes, theatre performances and cultural events highlighting the dangers of drug and substance abuse. Programmes promoting patriotism and national unity will also form an important part of the celebrations. The second day of the festival coincides with Teachers’ Day, and special programmes will be organised to honour teachers. The celebrations will conclude with a cultural evening at the iconic Mannan Top View Point at Lamochan. Various institutions and departments, including Power Grid Corporation, the Army, BRO and other government departments, are supporting the initiative.
